test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 29 July, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following relationship between the sets of integers, rational numbers, and real numbers holds good?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Numbers follow a hierarchical inclusion: Natural ⊆ Whole ⊆ Integers ⊆ Rationals ⊆ Reals.

Every Integer (Z) can be expressed as a fraction Z/1, so Z is a subset of Rational numbers (Q).

The set of Real numbers (R) includes all Rational (Q) and Irrational numbers.

Thus, the nested relationship is Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.

**∴ The correct answer is Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sets Z (Integers), Q (Rational Numbers), and R (Real Numbers).

**Property:** A ⊆ B means every element of set A is contained within set B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b608a81024f893ba20589f8e55e90ea098d69db9a86a2c505cbb4757298d9f8.png] 

⇒ Integers (Z) = {..., −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, ...}

⇒ Rational Numbers (Q) = {p/q : p, q ∈ Z, q ≠ 0}

⇒ Since any integer n = n/1, every integer is a rational number ∴ Z ⊆ Q.

⇒ Real Numbers (R) consist of all points on the number line (Rational ∪ Irrational).

⇒ Since all rational numbers are part of the real number line ∴ Q ⊆ R.

⇒ Combining these: Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.

**∴ The correct answer is Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.**

**__Additional Information__**

Natural Numbers (N)

The set {1, 2, 3, ...} is the most basic subset of integers, denoted as N ⊆ Z.

Irrational Numbers (I)

Numbers like √2, π, and e that cannot be written as p/q. Note that Q ∩ I = ∅ and Q ∪ I = R.

Complex Numbers (C)

The set of numbers in the form a + bi, where a and b are real numbers and i = √−1. R is a subset of C (R ⊆ C).</p
